cost: THE SUBJECT LANDS ON HIS BAND'S EDGE, 65 against 62 +-3, AND 65 IS THE FLOOR OF WHAT IS REACHABLE. The frontier is Nenê '11 (recal_139, off 66 +-2, reading 65 before the round) at 30.5 minutes against the subject's 29.2: any factor monotone in minutes pays him about what it pays the subject. Swept over the whole line: the subject reads 65 from 33.4 to 34.3 and never lower, and at 34.4 Nenê leaves his band. Reaching 62 itself would need both terms zeroed for him, because recal_118's off-ball-floor correction damps every further o_score point he loses by 0.84.
A NEW ANCHOR: Richaun Holmes '21 off 62 +-3 (round 163), pinned at the number the ruling names rather than at the 65 reached. 155 anchors, 0 failing.

THE FOOTPRINT: 93 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM DOWN, mean -2.38, max -10; 70 OVRs follow; DEF, every attribute and every card above the 93 knee are byte-identical, and the top 12 by OFF is unchanged with no rank flip touching the top 50 by OVR. Every mover is a big (or, in Kevin Gamble '91's case, a wing inside is_big) who took recal_107's or recal_112's term. data/build_ratings.py is untouched.

TWO DEVIATION TAXES MOVED, on OPPOSITE edges, and this is the mirror of rounds 154/155: a round that LOWERS 93 offensive cards makes the default plan weaker, so a blind call costs less (hunt went over the blind ceiling at 3.85, -0.2123) and the oracle call is worth less of a smaller number (crash def glass went under the oracle floor at 0.72, +0.4855). Each was swept ONCE from main's constant and set at its true midpoint by recal_126's rule: hunt 3.85 -> 3.99 (feasible 3.953-4.024, a NARROW 0.071), crashDef 0.72 -> 0.58 (feasible 0.492-0.676). crash off held at 0.55 and the six others held their bands. All nine rows pass. This is hunt's fourteenth move.

STILL OPEN, and it belongs to whoever reads this term next: the second-payment load line is a NEW line in this file (SECOND_FULL = 33.9) and recal_130's own second line for the elite passer is 34.7, measured the same way on a different class. Two classes, two quartiles, two constants — if a later round unifies them it should do it by re-measuring, not by averaging.
TEAM DIALS: src/data/campaigns.json moved one tier line and src/data/opponents.json six; no five's dial moved enough to change a tier's difficulty band, and no team anchor (rank or dial) fails.
notes: WHAT THE RULING WAS REALLY ABOUT, decomposed on the card. Richaun Holmes '21, 29.2 minutes, 17.0% usage, 14.2 points: o_score standard path 62.656, recal_107's two-level premium +9.520, recal_112's efficient-interior term +8.811, total 80.99 x 0.93 = OFF 75. Against his own '20 the standard path moved 56.8 -> 62.7 and the other +18.3 was these two terms turning on together - mid 56 -> 76 crossed recal_107's gate 0.07 -> 1.00 and efficiency 83 -> 89 crossed recal_112's 85 foot - on a season whose true shooting went DOWN, .681 -> .669. Round 112's receipt checked non-stacking on ONE card, Deandre Ayton '26, where one of the two gates was shut, so the stack was never measured on a card that clears both.

WHY THE TWO TERMS OVERLAP BY CONSTRUCTION, which is what makes the fix a formula and not a patch: recal_107's efficiency ramp SATURATES at 85 and recal_112's efficiency ramp BEGINS at 85. Above 85 both terms are paid, in full, for one man's conversion - the pair is a single claim (this big's interior scoring is underpaid) charged twice. recal_117 ruled the cure for exactly this shape one term up the file ("the product of two decreasing factors is steeper than either ... READ THE CLAIM ONCE") and recal_139 applied it inside recal_112 itself.

SIX CARDS OF 10,000 TAKE BOTH TERMS and they are the whole of clause 1's footprint: Kevin Gamble '91, Richaun Holmes '21, Serge Ibaka '13, Brad Miller '03, '04 and '05. 48 cards take recal_107 alone, 151 take recal_112 alone, and for every one of them `_tl_add` is zero or `_ef` is zero and the max() is the identity.

WHY BOTH CLAUSES, measured on the whole pool, neither decorative: clause 1 alone (one claim, one payment) leaves the subject on 67, outside his band; clause 2 alone (both terms at the second-payment load line, still added together) leaves him on 72. Together, 65. Clause 2 is also what carries the round beyond the six stacking cards, and it is the same doctrine recal_130 wrote for the elite passer: a rate the standard path already paid is being paid a second time, and the second payment cannot take recal_96's 24-minute bench line, which every rotation big clears.

THE LINE IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN, by recal_130's own method: of the 193 cards these two terms pay, the 75th percentile of minutes is 33.9 (p25 27.2, median 31.1). The share is recal_96's own ramp off its own foot, (mpg - 12) / (33.9 - 12), clipped - so the round introduces no constant but the measured line, and a card with no minutes on the sheet takes 1.0, which is recal_96's "measured, or not at all".

REJECTED, all measured on the whole pool against every anchor: the geometric mean of the two terms (recal_139's own combination) and the min both leave the subject at 66-67 without a load line and land on the same 65 with one, so the max() is taken because it is the only one of the three with a sentence behind it - the second payment is paid on what the first left unpaid. A flat share min(1, mpg / 33.9) instead of recal_96's ramp leaves him on 66. Re-deriving OFF_TOP was never considered: recal_90's warning is that it moves every card above the knee, and this round moves nobody there.

NOTHING IN THE ROUND IS A PER-PLAYER OVERRIDE. Both clauses are evaluated on every card in the pool; the subject is reached by what the class function does to his minutes and his two gates, and his name appears in the code only in the comment that records the ruling.
